name: sleep-spawning
comment: WP-2.3: SpawnerAnimals.performSleepSpawning. A closed stone room (outer x, z -4..4, y 59..66; inner air x, z -3..3, y 61..64), no light source inside, under a layer of still water (y 67) so that no column on the roof is a monster spot (the feet would be in a liquid); every block lies within 24 blocks of the player, so performSpawning never reaches a constructor and the only hostile constructors are the sleep spawn's, whose EntityMob.getCanSpawnHere light rolls on the unseeded rand (census §3) then always pass (sky and block light 0 inside, dumped at t = 100). Night from t = 0 (set_time 18000); at t = 2 the player right-clicks the bed (foot (0, 61, 2), head (0, 61, 3)): BlockBed.blockActivated, EntityPlayer.sleepInBedAt. After 100 ticks fully asleep World.tick runs performSleepSpawning (difficulty 1, hostile spawning on): up to 20 tries at random columns within 32 blocks, a spider, zombie or skeleton (nightSpawnEntities[nextInt(3)]) placed with a World.rand yaw, the Pathfinder from it to the player (range 32), and if the path ends within 1.5 blocks of the player the monster moves next to the bed (BlockBed.getNearestEmptyChunkCoordinates), joins, wakes the player and makes its living sound; otherwise the night is skipped (world time to the next multiple of 24000) and every player woken. The run stops before t = 103, where the oracle's skeleton shoots its first arrow (new EntityArrow(world, skeleton): setArrowHeading's jitter on the arrow's unseeded rand, census §3, would make the trace irreproducible). rng_state, entity_state all and world_time every tick.
